articles.body:
[q="MrEleven"]This might sound like a dumb question but I am trying to be as technical as possible here.  King Arthur's hero card says:
[q]"When King Arthur attacks, you may BOOST that attack. Play the BOOST card, face down, along with your attack card. [b][u]If your opponent cancels the effects on your attack card[/u][/b], the BOOST is discarded without effect."[/q]

If you were to attack with Excalibur and boost it, then your opponent plays Feint, would it really make you discard your boost card?  Excalibur [b][u]doesn't have any effects[/u][/b] on it, thus Feint technically [b][u]did not cancel any effects[/u][/b], thus it would seem that King Arthur shouldn't have to discard his boost card in this one rare case.  Is this a legitimate reading of King Arthur's power?[/q]

Congratulations, you were right all these years ago. They just announced they are changing the official rules to go by this interpretation in their discord.
